title: Spiralling charges
metaphor: A charge in a magnetic field is like a figure skater on a rope: pulled sideways at every moment, it circles while gliding forward.
hook: Aurora curtains follow field lines because charged particles refuse to cross them freely.
why_care: Your particle pusher must resolve this circling motion, or the simulated energy drifts away from physical values.

blocks.text: The Larmor radius is the radius of the circular part of that helix and grows with the particle speed.
blocks.meaning: Seen from above the particle draws a circle; along the field it slides forward. The [[Larmor radius]] is the size of that circle.

blocks.caption: The circle gets wider with speed and tighter with a stronger field.

symbols.meaning: the speed across the field lines
mass and charge of the particle

blocks.text: How often the particle goes around is the [[gyrofrequency]]. It depends on the charge, the mass and the field strength, not on the speed, which is why a fast and a slow ion of the same kind finish each circle in the same time even though the fast one draws a wider one.

blocks.title: How a helix appears
blocks.caption: Two independent motions add up: a circle across the field and a free slide along it.

blocks.text: Apply an electric field across the magnetic field and the circles drift sideways. This is the [[E cross B drift]].

items.title: Same for both
items.text: Electrons and ions drift with the same velocity, so this drift alone carries no net current.

items.title: Field gradient
items.text: A magnetic field that changes in space adds a slow sideways drift of its own.

quiz.question: You double the speed $v_\perp$ of an ion in a uniform magnetic field. What happens to the radius $r_L$ of its circle?
quiz.explain_right: The Larmor radius grows with the particle speed, so $2 v_\perp$ gives a circle with $r_L$ twice as large.
quiz.explain_wrong: Recall which quantity grows with speed and which depends only on charge, mass and field.

glossary.definition: The radius of the circular part of a charged particle's spiral path in a magnetic field.
How many times per second a charged particle circles a magnetic field line.
The sideways drift of charged particles when electric and magnetic fields cross at right angles.

key_takeaways: In a magnetic field a charge moves along a helix whose circle size is the Larmor radius.
Adding a crossed electric field makes the circles drift at the E cross B velocity.
